title: Banking
intro: These ten role plays each run 16–20 lines, end in a clear resolution, and cover account queries, cards, digital banking, loans, fees, complaints and vulnerable customers. Pair trainees as Officer and Customer, run the scene once as written, then again without the script.

criteria.name: Listening and clarifying
levels: Paraphrases and confirms names, numbers and dates unprompted

criteria.name: Clear explanation
levels: One idea per sentence, checks understanding

criteria.name: Empathy and tone
levels: Acknowledges, apologises where right, then acts

criteria.name: Process accuracy
levels: Asks for PIN or OTP, or over-promises

criteria.name: Resolution and next steps
levels: States what, who and when, with a reference number

debrief: Which sentence did the Customer find most reassuring, and why?
Where did the Officer sound scripted, and how could that line be said more naturally?
What one phrase from the scene would you add to your own daily vocabulary?
If this Customer were angrier or more frightened, what would you change first?

scenarios.title: Opening a savings account
scenarios.setting: Kavindi, 22, has just started her first job and needs a salary account by Friday.
scenarios.resolution: The account is open and the number is in the customer's hands. One follow-up document (the address declaration) is agreed with a clear next step.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The spelling of the customer's name on her NIC differs from her employment letter. The officer must explain the problem politely and agree the fix.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: requesting documents politely, explaining conditions, checking understanding.

lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to Island Commercial Bank. How may I help you?
Good morning. I'd like to open a savings account. I've just started my first job.
Congratulations! Is the account for your salary?
Yes. My employer needs my account number by Friday.
That's fine. May I see your National Identity Card, please?
Here it is. Do I need anything else?
Yes, I'll also need your employment letter and proof of your address, such as a recent utility bill.
I have the letter, but our electricity bill is in my father's name.
That's acceptable if your father signs a short declaration. I'll give you the form now.
Thank you. Is there a minimum balance?
Not on the Salary Saver account, as long as your salary is credited every month.
Good. Can I use mobile banking too?
Yes. You'll set your own password in the app. Please never share it, or any OTP, with anyone.
Understood. And a debit card?
It will be ready in about five working days. Please collect it with your NIC.
Wonderful. What happens next?
Please sign here and here. Your account is now open, and your account number is on this slip.
Thank you. I'll send the number to my employer today and bring the declaration tomorrow.

scenarios.title: Accessing a late spouse's account
scenarios.setting: Mrs. Fernando, 68, lost her husband two weeks ago. They held a joint account that allows either holder or the survivor to operate it.
scenarios.resolution: The account is updated, the customer has her cash, and a follow-up call is booked for the remaining accounts.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The main account is in the husband's name alone. The officer must explain that the bank needs more documents, without alarming the customer, and still offer a concrete next step. No product selling in this scene.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: condolence phrases, slow and simple explanations, avoiding jargon, giving the customer control of the pace.

lines.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Fernando. Please have a seat. How can I help you today?
Good afternoon. My husband passed away two weeks ago. I don't know what to do about our account.
I'm very sorry for your loss. Please take your time. I'll guide you step by step.
Thank you. The electricity bill is due, and I'm not sure I'm allowed to take money out now.
I understand. This is a joint account, and the instruction says either holder or the survivor may operate it. So yes, you can, once we record the death.
What do you need from me?
The original death certificate and your National Identity Card. We'll copy them and return the originals today.
I have both here. Please take them.
Thank you. This will take about ten minutes. Would you like some water while you wait?
Yes, please. I'm sorry, I'm a little tired.
Please don't apologise. Here you are. All done: your husband's name is recorded, and the account now continues in your name.
So I can withdraw money for the bill today?
Yes, of course. How much would you like?
Twelve thousand rupees, please.
Please sign this slip. Here is your cash, and here are your original documents.
Thank you. Is there anything else I must do?
Possibly. If he had other accounts or deposits in his name alone, they may need legal documents. Our branch manager will explain, and I'll call you tomorrow to fix a time. Is this the right number?
Yes. Thank you for being so kind.

scenarios.title: Lost debit card
scenarios.setting: Mr. Kumar, working in Kandy, has lost his wallet on a bus. The card and his NIC were inside.
scenarios.resolution: The card is blocked, the customer knows no unauthorised use has occurred, a replacement is ordered, and the lost NIC is handled with a clear plan.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer is on a noisy bus, speaks quickly, and cannot remember his registered mobile number. The officer must find another verification route and keep the customer calm.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: calm telephone openings, verification questions, spelling out reference numbers, confirming next steps.

lines.text: Good evening, Island Commercial Bank hotline. How may I help you?
Hello. I've lost my wallet, and my debit card was in it. Please block it!
I'm sorry to hear that, sir. I'll block it right away. First, may I verify your identity? Your full name and NIC number, please.
Suresh Kumar. My NIC number is (gives number).
Thank you. Now your date of birth and the last four digits of your registered mobile number, please. I will never ask for your PIN.
(gives details) Please hurry.
Thank you, Mr. Kumar, you're verified. I'm blocking the card now. It is done: the card ending 4821 is blocked.
Has anyone used it?
Let me check. I can see one purchase of 1,850 rupees at a pharmacy at 4.10 p.m. Do you recognise it?
Yes, that was me. I lost the wallet after that.
Good. No further transactions are possible on that card. I can order a replacement for pickup at a branch in about five working days. Which branch is convenient?
The Kandy branch, please. My NIC was also in the wallet. What should I do?
Please report the lost NIC to the police. Bring the report to the branch so we can verify you another way.
I'll go to the police station tomorrow morning.
Good. Let me confirm: your card is blocked, the new one will be ready at the Kandy branch in five working days, and your reference number is LC-20481.
Could you repeat the reference number slowly?
Of course. L-C, two, zero, four, eight, one. I'll also send it by SMS.
I've received it. Thank you for your quick help.
You're welcome, Mr. Kumar. Please call us any time.

scenarios.title: ATM debited, no cash dispensed
scenarios.setting: Mr. Perera is upset. An ATM kept his withdrawal request but gave him no cash, and he needs money for his daughter's school fees.
scenarios.resolution: The dispute is registered with a reference number, a realistic timeline is set, and the customer has a practical way to cover his urgent need today.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer demands an instant refund and threatens to post about the bank online. The officer must stay calm, avoid promises the bank cannot keep, and keep returning to what can be done today.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: acknowledge, apologise, act; asking precise questions; setting honest expectations without over-promising.

lines.text: I need to speak to someone now. Your ATM took my money and gave me nothing!
I'm very sorry, sir. Please sit down, and I'll look into it with you right away. May I have your name?
Dilshan Perera. I tried to withdraw ten thousand rupees at your Maharagama ATM this morning.
Thank you, Mr. Perera. About what time was that, and did the machine show an error message?
Around nine-thirty. The screen said "Please wait", then the card came out. No cash, no receipt.
That must have been stressful. Let me check your account. Yes, I can see a debit of ten thousand rupees at 9.34 a.m.
So where is my money? I need it today for my daughter's school fees.
I understand it's urgent. We must check the machine's records to confirm that no cash was dispensed. This protects you and the bank.
How long will that take?
In most cases the amount is returned within five working days. I'll register the dispute now and mark it urgent.
Five days is too long. The fees are due on Wednesday.
I hear you. Let me speak to my supervisor about what we can do. Please give me two minutes.
Okay, I'll wait.
Thank you for waiting. Our ATM team will check the machine records today, and we'll tell you the result by tomorrow evening. If your balance allows, you can withdraw the amount at the counter now.
That helps. And if the machine really gave no cash?
Then the ten thousand rupees returns to your account automatically. You don't need to do anything.
Alright. Thank you. I'm sorry I was upset earlier.
No need to apologise. Your reference is ATM-3317, and we'll send the result by SMS tomorrow.

scenarios.title: Transfer debited, not credited
scenarios.setting: Mrs. Rizwan sent Rs. 50,000 to a supplier through the app. Her account was debited, but the supplier says nothing arrived.
scenarios.resolution: The customer learns the cause (a mistyped digit), confirms her money is safe, and completes the correct transfer with the officer's guidance.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The status shows "pending" instead of "returned". The officer must explain that the bank is tracing the payment with the other bank, give a realistic update time, and never guess the outcome.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: guiding someone through app steps, reading numbers aloud, explaining a technical status in plain words, protecting security details.

lines.text: Good morning, digital banking support. How can I help you?
Hello. I sent fifty thousand rupees to my supplier last night through the app. My account was debited, but he says he hasn't received it.
I'm sorry for the worry, madam. May I verify you first? Your full name and the last four digits of your registered mobile number, please.
Fathima Rizwan, and the last four digits are 5-0-7-2.
Thank you, Mrs. Rizwan. What time did you send it, and which bank does your supplier use?
About 9.40 p.m. He banks with another bank in Colombo.
Thank you. Please give me a moment to check. I can see the transfer. The receiving bank rejected it, and the full amount returned to your account at 9.52 p.m.
Rejected? Why?
The account number did not match an open account at the receiving bank. A digit may have been entered incorrectly. Could you check it with your supplier's message?
Let me look. Yes, I typed one digit wrongly. But is my money really back?
Yes. Your balance shows the returned fifty thousand rupees. Nothing was lost.
What a relief! Can you help me send it again? I'm afraid I'll make another mistake.
Of course. I'll guide you, but you will enter the details yourself. Please open the app, go to "Transfers", then "Other bank". Tell me when you're there.
I'm there.
Now type the account number from your supplier's message. Please read me only the last four digits.
Three, one, four, nine.
Good. Check it against his message once more, then confirm. You'll receive an OTP. Please keep it to yourself.
Done. The app says the transfer was successful.
Wonderful. Please ask your supplier to check his account in a few minutes.
I will. Thank you so much for your patience.

scenarios.title: OTP shared with a scammer
scenarios.setting: Mr. Jayasinghe received a call from someone claiming to be "card department staff" and read out an OTP. Two transfers followed within minutes.
scenarios.resolution: Further losses are stopped, the fraud case is opened with a reference, and the customer leaves with three clear actions: police report, branch visit, and wait for the fraud team's call.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer blames the bank and demands a full refund on the spot. The officer must acknowledge his anger, explain the investigation honestly, and avoid any promise of an outcome.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: calm, directive language in an emergency, non-judgmental explanation, honest limits ("I can't promise, but..."), clear next steps.

lines.text: Hello! Someone has taken money from my account! Please help me!
Please stay calm, sir. I'll help you right now. May I have your full name and NIC number?
Nuwan Jayasinghe. My NIC number is (gives number).
Thank you. Please tell me exactly what happened, from the start.
A man called me and said he was from the bank's card department. He said my card needed an upgrade and sent me an OTP. I read it to him. Then I got two SMS about transfers.
Thank you. Our first priority is to stop any more losses. I'm locking your mobile banking and your debit card now. Please stay on the line.
Please do it fast.
Done. Both are locked. I can see two transfers, of eighty thousand and sixty thousand rupees, in the last fifteen minutes. Are those the ones you received SMS about?
Yes! That's one hundred and forty thousand. Is it gone?
I've flagged both transfers as fraud and asked the receiving banks to hold the funds. I can't promise they can be recovered, but acting quickly helps.
How could this happen? I thought it was the bank calling.
Fraudsters imitate banks very well. Please remember: we will never ask for your OTP, PIN or password, by phone or message.
I feel so stupid.
Please don't blame yourself. These callers are skilled, and many people are caught. What matters is that you called quickly.
What happens now?
Please report this to the police today. Our fraud team will investigate and contact you within two working days.
And my card and the app?
They stay locked until you visit the branch with your NIC to reset them safely. Your reference number is FR-5520.
Thank you. I'll go to the police and the branch tomorrow.

scenarios.title: Personal loan explained
scenarios.setting: Mr. Wickramasinghe wants Rs. 1,000,000 to renovate his house and asks how the loan works. The rate, fee and timelines below are illustrative.
scenarios.resolution: The customer understands the instalment, total cost, fees and the variable-rate risk, chooses 36 months, and leaves with a document list and an honest timeline.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer says another bank offers a lower rate and accuses this bank of hiding fees. The officer must compare total cost openly, without criticising the competitor.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: saying figures and percentages aloud, "about" and "roughly", explaining a variable rate, "may" versus "will", refusing to guarantee approval.

lines.text: Good morning. I'd like a loan of one million rupees to renovate my house. Can you explain how it works?
Certainly, Mr. Wickramasinghe. I'll go through the main points, and please stop me if anything is unclear. How long would you like to repay over?
Maybe three years.
Over 36 months, at our current rate of 14 percent a year, your monthly instalment would be about thirty-four thousand, one hundred and seventy-eight rupees.
And how much will I pay in total?
About 1.23 million rupees. So the interest is roughly 230,000 rupees over three years.
Is the interest rate fixed?
No, it is a variable rate. It follows market rates, so it can go up or down, and your instalment may change. We will inform you before any change.
Are there any other charges?
Yes. There is a processing fee of one percent, which is ten thousand rupees, deducted when the loan is released. A late payment charge applies if an instalment is missed.
What if I want to pay it off early?
You can settle early, but an early settlement fee may apply. I'll mark it on the fee sheet. Please read the loan agreement fully before you sign.
Would a 48-month loan make the instalment smaller?
Yes, it would be lower, but you would pay more interest in total.
Then I'll stay with 36 months. What do you need from me?
Your NIC, your last three salary slips, three months of bank statements, and a quotation from your contractor. We will also check your credit report.
Will my loan definitely be approved?
I can't guarantee it, because approval depends on the assessment. If your documents are complete, you will usually hear from us within five working days.
Thank you. That was very clear. I'll bring the documents tomorrow.

scenarios.title: Unexpected monthly charge
scenarios.setting: Mrs. Ranasinghe has noticed a Rs. 500 "service charge" on her statement for three months running. Fee amounts and the goodwill decision are illustrative.
scenarios.resolution: The customer understands why the charge applied, receives a goodwill refund for one month, and moves to an account that suits her balance, with no further charges.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer insists a staff member promised her there would be no charges. The officer must neither confirm nor dismiss the claim, check the account notes, and escalate it properly.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: explaining policy without blaming, offering options, saying "no" kindly, goodwill wording.

lines.text: Good afternoon. Why is money taken from my account every month? My statement says "account service charge".
Good afternoon, Mrs. Ranasinghe. Let me look at your account so I can explain. May I see your NIC, please?
Here. It's five hundred rupees each month, for three months now.
Thank you. I can see a monthly service charge of five hundred rupees. It applies when the average monthly balance falls below twenty-five thousand rupees.
Nobody told me about that when I opened the account.
I'm sorry if it wasn't explained clearly. It is in the fee schedule, but I understand it is easy to miss. Here is the page.
My balance only dropped because I paid my son's university fees.
That is a large expense, and I understand. Let me check what options we have. Please give me a moment.
Alright.

There are two options. You can keep this account and keep the average balance above twenty-five thousand, and no charge will apply. Or you can move to our Basic Saver account, which has no minimum balance and no monthly service charge.
Does Basic Saver pay the same interest?
The rate is a little lower. I'll show you both rates on this sheet, so you can compare.
And the charges I've already paid?

They were applied under the fee schedule, so I can't reverse all three. But my supervisor has agreed, as a goodwill gesture, to refund the most recent month, five hundred rupees. It will appear within two working days.
Only one month? Well, that's better than nothing.
I understand your disappointment. If you move to Basic Saver today, no further charge will apply. Would you like to do that?
Yes, let's switch. Will my account number stay the same?
Yes, it will. Please sign here. I'll also give you the new fee sheet, and you'll get an SMS confirming the change.
Thank you. I'm glad you explained it properly.

scenarios.title: Formal complaint and escalation
scenarios.setting: Mr. Gunawardena's standing order for an insurance premium failed, he wasn't told, and his policy lapsed. Two earlier phone calls produced no follow-up. He now wants a formal complaint. Reference numbers and timelines are illustrative.
scenarios.resolution: The complaint is formally recorded, summarised and confirmed with the customer, he knows the process and his escalation rights, and he leaves with a reference number and a named contact.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer is angry, interrupts, and demands the manager. The officer must stay composed, still complete the written record, and offer a manager's call-back time.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: formal register, summarising to confirm understanding, recording the outcome the customer wants, explaining escalation rights accurately, repairing trust.

notes.label: Accuracy note
notes.text: The Central Bank's complaint system asks customers to raise the complaint with the financial institution first, and to escalate only if it remains unresolved or the response is unsatisfactory (CBSL announcement, 15 May 2026). Check the exact timelines and wording against your own bank's complaints procedure.

lines.text: Good morning. I want to make a formal complaint. I have called twice already and nothing has happened.
Good morning, Mr. Gunawardena. I'm sorry you've had to come back. I'll record this as a formal complaint today. May I start by hearing what happened?
In August my standing order for my life insurance premium failed, and the bank didn't tell me. The policy lapsed, and now I must pay a reinstatement fee.
Thank you. Do you remember the date and the amount of the failed payment?
The fifth of August. Fifteen thousand rupees.
Let me summarise. The standing order due on 5 August for fifteen thousand rupees failed, you weren't informed, and the policy lapsed. Have I understood correctly?
Yes, exactly. And my two calls were never followed up.
I've added that. What outcome would you like?
I want the bank to cover the reinstatement fee and explain why I wasn't notified.

Understood. I'm recording both requests. Now let me explain what happens next. You'll receive a written acknowledgement and a reference number today. Our complaints unit will review the case and send you a written reply within the timeline in our complaints procedure, which is printed on the acknowledgement.
And if I'm not satisfied?

Then you have the right to take it further. If our final response does not resolve the matter, you can escalate to the Central Bank through its online complaint system, or approach the Financial Ombudsman.
Good to know. I was beginning to think the bank doesn't care.
I understand why you feel that, and I'm sorry your earlier calls weren't followed up. I'll personally ask the complaints unit to find out why.
Thank you. Who will contact me?
A complaints officer will call you to confirm they have started the review. I'll also give you my direct number.
Please give me both the reference and your number.
Here is your acknowledgement. The reference is CMP-1042, and my number is written beneath it. If you haven't heard from us within a week, please call me.
Thank you. At least now something is in writing.

scenarios.title: Elderly customer and a prize scam
scenarios.setting: Mr. Jayasekara, 74, is hard of hearing. He wants to transfer Rs. 450,000 to "pay the tax" on a prize he believes he won through a WhatsApp message.
scenarios.resolution: The transfer is cancelled, the customer's savings are protected, and he leaves with a safeguard he agreed to (a daily limit) and a number to call.
scenarios.makeItHarder: The customer insists, "It's my money." The officer must respect his right to decide, record that the risk was explained, bring in the branch manager, and leave the door open for him to return.

notes.label: Language focus
notes.text: slow, clear speech; open questions; protecting dignity; explaining a scam without blame; respecting the customer's right to decide.

lines.text: Good morning. I want to send four hundred and fifty thousand rupees to this account. Here are the details.
Good morning, Mr. Jayasekara. Please have a seat. I'll speak slowly, so please tell me if I'm too quiet. This is a large amount. May I ask what it is for?
It's for taxes. I won a prize of eight million rupees, and they said I must pay the tax first.
That sounds exciting. How did you hear about the prize?
A message came on WhatsApp from a company. A very polite young man also phoned me.
Thank you for telling me. Did you enter a competition or buy a ticket?
No, but they said my phone number was selected.
I want to be honest with you, because I care about your savings. What you describe is a very common scam. A real prize never asks you to pay money first.
But they sent me a certificate with an official stamp.
Scammers make very convincing documents, and many careful people have been caught. It is not your fault. Before we send anything, may I suggest one safe check?
What check?
If the prize is real, it can wait one day. Could your daughter look at the message with you first?
She lives in Kandy. I can call her now.
Please do. I'll hold the transfer until you return, and I'll note the caller's number so we can report it.
I called her. She says the same as you: it's a trick.
I'm glad you called her. I know this is disappointing. Would you like to cancel the transfer?
Yes, please cancel it. I almost lost my savings.
You didn't, because you asked. If anyone calls again, hang up and don't send money. If you agree, I can also set a daily limit on your transfers, and here is a card with our branch number.
Thank you, young lady. I'm very grateful.
